People: Cadwallader Colden (author, Wikidata Q2932793), died 1776. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Colden, Cadwallader, 1688-1776") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: The history of the Five Indian Nations of Canada, which are dependent on the province of New-York in America, and are the barrier between the English and French in that part of the world [microform] : with accounts of their religion, manners, customs, laws, and forms of government ; their several battles and treaties with the European nations ; particular relations of their several wars with the other Indians ; and a true account of the present state of our trade with them : in which are shewn the great advantage of their trade and alliance to the British nation, and the intrigues and attempts of the French to engage them from us ; a subject nearly concerning all our American plantations, and highly meriting the consideration of the British nation at this juncture : to which are added accounts of the several other nations of Indians in North America ... and the treaties which have been lately made with them : a work highly entertaining to all, and particularly useful to the persons who have any trade or concern in that part of of [sic] the world, London : Printed for T. Osborne ..., 1747, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/cihm_33241. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 56%, 36%, 58% of their four-word runs in the scan's text.
